registration.log: PROJECT_LOG §2C 2026-10-16 (registered before any code) and its amendment (before any run)
registration.question: does fine-tuning the decoder on the prediction task (loss on measured HRTF) change the geometry result?
registration.encoder: FFM48k_measim (frozen; z targets as in FFM_3_8)
registration.subjects: 164 SONICOM development subjects, FFM_3_2_1 folds; development only (locked 36 spent 10-12)
registration.inputs: held-out rows: kernel ridge fitted on the fold's training subjects (FFM_3_8); training rows: cross-fitted within the training subjects (5 groups, the fold's alpha); constant input (R2) cross-fitted likewise

variants.A (primary): decoder FiLM row of measured SONICOM: per-bin gamma and beta, out' = exp(d)*(out - beta) + beta + db
variants.D (secondary): A + all decoder weights, L2-SP towards the pretrained weights

registration.training: each outer fold, training subjects only; 20% of them as inner validation, early stopping by LSD; loss = MSE (dB) over bins 1-85, elevation >= -45 deg; settings in FT
registration.gate: R0, R1 and the simulation row reproduce FFM_3_8 development LSD >= -45 deg (4.558, 4.378, 4.316 dB)
registration.primary: per variant, A primary: Delta = [LSD(R3) - LSD(R2)] - [LSD(R1) - LSD(R0)], per subject, paired bootstrap 2000
registration.reading: |Delta| < 1% of the mean LSD (~0.046 dB) or CI includes 0: the frozen decoder is not the limit; Delta <= -0.046 dB with CI below 0: fine-tuning adds geometry information. R2 - R0 and R4 descriptive.
